questions.question: What makes a good thesis statement?
options: It is specific, arguable and expressed in one sentence
It is vague so it can cover everything
It is a question to the reader
It is an announcement like "In this essay I will write about..."
questions.explanation: A strong thesis is specific, arguable and concise — not a vague announcement of the topic.

questions.question: What does PEEL stand for in paragraph structure?
questions.explanation: PEEL paragraphs make a Point, give Evidence, Explain the significance and Link back to the thesis.

questions.question: How much time does the chapter recommend spending on planning before writing the long answer?
questions.explanation: Spending around 15 minutes planning prevents the common mistake of jumping straight into writing without structure.

questions.question: What is the difference between an argumentative and a discursive essay?
options: Argumentative defends one position; discursive explores multiple perspectives
questions.explanation: An argumentative essay takes and defends a position, while a discursive essay explores several perspectives on an issue.

questions.question: Which qualities are examiners looking for in a long answer?
options: Clear structure, relevant content, varied vocabulary and coherence
As many difficult words as possible regardless of meaning
questions.explanation: Examiners reward clear structure, relevance, varied and precise language, correct grammar, coherence and a personal voice.
